text: The next Wednesday, every screen in the Hunter Association's lobby plays His Summons Go First. Twenty million views.
Jaeha is here for a hearing. Borro has to bend double to fit through the security arch.
A guard leans in to inspect one of the famous unusual husks.
He pokes Nib's cheek. Nib's eye twitches.
It's warm. Why is a husk warm? Jaeha smiles far too hard. They keep him by the heater.
Nib holds perfectly still while one bead of sweat rolls out from under his mask.
And the big one? A harmless husk, sir. He gardens.
In the hearing room: Mok with a lawyer, Jaeha alone with his two stiff husks, and a packed gallery.
Inspector Ryu opens the hearing: Gate 0912, and Mr. Kang Jaeha's so-called unusual husks.
Black Hound's lawyer keeps it simple. Jaeha set off the hidden boss, and four hunters died because of it.
Mok lays a hand on his heart, eyes glistening for the cameras. He shut that door to save his team.
In the gallery, Yerin grips the rail until her knuckles go white.
Did Jaeha enter the boss room on his own? He bows politely. He followed orders. Summons first, then summoners.
Then Choi testifies. The boss room's lamp was red, so the boss was above the gate's grade. Black Hound's paid survey said C-grade.
He holds up the photo: the iron door, the lamp burning red.
An F-rank and a rookie walked out of a gate that killed four B-ranks. And Black Hound postponed the market gate twice.
The lawyer leaps up. Objection! The market break isn't what this hearing is about.
Too late. Every reporter in the room is typing.
Then Yerin takes the stand, small behind the microphone. It was her first raid.
The lawyer smiles kindly and goes for the throat. She froze on that raid. How does she know what she saw?
Her eyes fill, then steady. She froze. She wasn't blind.
She points straight across the room at Mok. She watched him close that door, with them on the wrong side of it.
Nobody moves. Every face in the room turns to Mok.
Under the table, his knuckles go white.
In the recess, Yerin is shaking. Why doesn't Jaeha just play them his recording of Mok's bribe?
Because a bribe only gets Mok a fine. Jaeha wants him for the door.
The testimony conflicts, so the panel will judge what it can see. Jaeha is re-tested today, in the arena, with his husks.
Mok smiles again. Good. Let everyone see what a husk really is.
Behind Jaeha's chair, both husks stare straight ahead, sweating.
Noon, in the basement arena: a four-metre construct of granite and brass, with an amber test core glowing in its chest.
A window only Jaeha can see: his class, Operator, is hidden. Everyone else sees an F-rank summoner.
The rules: a B-grade construct, five minutes, and the test ends when its core is touched.
Jaeha reads that line twice. Touched. Not destroyed. Touched.
He reminds his summons: they're husks. Stiff, slow, silent, no field form. Borro is always slow. This will be easy.
The construct's stone head grinds round, and the clock starts.
Borro marches out like a wind-up toy soldier, far too fast and far too heavy, cracking the floor.
Nib walks out with his arms stuck out stiffly, flapping like a penguin.
Behind the observation glass, an evaluator drops his pen, and Choi buries his face in his hands. Are they dancing?
The construct swings at Borro, who takes it on his shield and skids back several metres on his heels, still frozen in his husk pose.
Jaeha flinches once as the blow lands in him too, and keeps his face blank.
Then he whispers the plan. Nib, between its legs. Touch the core. Just touch it.
Arms still stuck out, Nib darts straight between the construct's legs. No field form, but still a scout.
He runs up its leg, using the brass bands as rungs.
One finger taps the grille over the core.
The construct freezes mid-swing and goes dark. Nib drops to the floor and stands stiffly again, like a husk.
Core touched. Time: four seconds.
Behind the glass, nobody moves. Inspector Ryu's glasses slide down his nose. Mok's smile freezes.
Jaeha bows to the window. The rules said touched, sir. His husk touched it.
The lawyer protests: it didn't even fight! Inspector Ryu holds up the rule sheet. They wrote those rules. Nobody ever reads them.
Licence kept. Two unusual husks, registered to Kang Jaeha.
In the corridor, Mok smiles for the cameras. See you at the raid on Saturday, hero. Of course, sir. He'll walk in first, like always.
Mok squeezes his shoulder hard enough to crease the vest. Jaeha's hand hangs perfectly relaxed.
Behind him, Nib's hand drifts toward his knives.
Without looking, Jaeha catches Nib's wrist. Not here. Not yet.
Outside, reporters and fans crowd the steps, one of them holding a cardboard cut-out of a big husk.
Bomi is thrilled. Four seconds. Her chat is calling it the fastest re-test in history.
Nib flapping, Borro marching, and Jaeha behind them with his face in his hands.
Choi hands him a coffee, serious for once. Still going into Mok's raid after today? More than ever.
Then Jaeha stops, as if he can feel someone watching him.
Inside, behind the glass doors, Black Hound's crossbow hunter leans against a pillar with her arms folded, smiling straight at him.
She gives him a tiny wave.
He knows her. Mok's crossbow. She was right behind Mok when he closed the door.
In her palm sits a small brass compass with a glowing violet needle, swinging.
It slows, and settles, trembling, loosely toward the steps.
At Jaeha. There you are, she whispers.
